prompts: Create one photographic widescreen 16:9 production reference frame for a replacement opening shot in a live-action travel-cup commercial. Image 1 establishes the existing kitchen, stone counter, overcast window lighting and photographic color grade. Image 2 is the authoritative olive travel-cup geometry, color and charcoal lid. Preserve these. This is a distinct new close shot, not a collage. Camera is a 90mm close-focus lens, about 35 degrees above the stone countertop, very near the open cup. The lid has been removed and lies flat on the countertop just behind it, with its exact original profile and sip opening. A small clear glass coffee carafe enters naturally from upper right, supported by one anatomically correct adult female right hand with the oatmeal sleeve from Image 1. One narrow uninterrupted dark coffee stream pours from its spout into the open cup. The stream strikes the coffee surface inside, creating concentric ripples and a few small natural bubbles; liquid stays below the rim and nothing spills. We see the cup's upper half and taper, tactile matte olive finish, the curved coffee meniscus, real stone pores, slight steam only where the light catches it. No decorative splash, no frozen explosion, no extra utensils, no text, no logo. The coffee preparation is the visual event. Physically grounded shadows, believable glass refraction, organic liquid shapes, extremely realistic photographic surfaces, no CGI smoothness. Natural soft daylight and restrained neutral grade matching Image 1. Place the focus on the point where the coffee stream meets the liquid, with product rim and front wall also sharp. Product dominant, composition has depth rather than a flat catalogue view.

Create one photographic widescreen 16:9 production reference frame for a replacement closing shot in a live-action travel-cup commercial. Image 1 is the identity, hair, oatmeal shirt, denim jeans and photographic lighting/color reference; use the exact same adult woman. Image 2 fixes the olive travel cup proportions, matte body and charcoal lid with small rectangular sip opening. Preserve the cup and make it realistically handheld in her right hand. New scene: the entrance of the same believable Dutch home, with a simple wood front door already open onto a softly defocused residential street, diffuse overcast morning light beyond. Three-quarter side camera at waist level, 50mm lens, looking diagonally across the doorway. Frame from her shoulders to upper thighs. She is caught naturally mid-step across the threshold heading outside, torso turned toward the street, the cup held upright near her right hip in a normal secure grip, left hand resting naturally on the door edge as she passes it. Her right forearm and complete cup are the sharp foreground subject, with oatmeal fabric weave and believable folds. Cup large enough to read but correctly scaled to her fingers and torso, never oversized. No handbag, no coat, no new accessories, no props besides the door and cup, no visible labels or text. This frame must communicate departure and purpose, not somebody posing with a product. Real skin creases at the grip, soft contact shadows, subtle movement in shirt hem. Real photographic depth and soft exterior daylight, no artificial spotlight or heavy flare, no CGI, no mannequin anatomy. Keep spatial relationships simple and physically plausible so the scene can animate into one uninterrupted step through the open doorway.
